blocks.text: **The problem.** Given strings `s` and `t`, return the **shortest substring** of `s` that contains every character of `t`, counting duplicates (if t has two a's, the window needs two a's). If there is none, return `""`. The answer is unique when it exists.

blocks.alt: s is A D O B E C O D E B A N C and t is ABC. The first window that covers A, B and C is ADOBEC, at indexes 0 to 5, in yellow. Sliding on, the shortest covering window is BANC, at indexes 9 to 12, in green.

blocks.code:
s = "ADOBECODEBANC", t = "ABC"   ->  "BANC"
s = "a", t = "a"                 ->  "a"
s = "a", t = "aa"                ->  ""     (s has only one "a")

blocks.text: The idea: grow until it fits, then shrink while it still fits

This is the variable-size window, used to find the **shortest** valid window. Move `right` to take in characters until the window covers t. Then move `left` to drop characters for as long as the window **still** covers t, recording each covering window's length. When dropping a character breaks the cover, go back to growing. Every character enters once and leaves once.

The bookkeeping is what makes it O(1) per step. `need[ch]` says how many more copies of `ch` the window still lacks — it can go **below zero** when the window holds spare copies. `missing` is the total still lacking: the window covers t exactly when `missing == 0`, so there's never a need to compare whole count tables.
1. Brute force: the shortest covering window from every start
From each start, extend to the right until the window covers t; that's the shortest one from this start. Keep the best over all starts.
**Time O(n²), space O(1)** beyond the answer (the counters have 128 slots, for ASCII). Each start rescans the characters the previous start already counted.

blocks.caption: Grow until missing is 0, then shrink while it stays 0; the green window is the best so far.

blocks.text: **Time O(n + m), space O(1)** for n = |s| and m = |t|: counting t is O(m), and `left` and `right` each pass over s once. (The Java and C++ versions use a 128-slot array instead of a map: characters outside t simply go negative and never matter.)

rows.approach: Brute force: the shortest covering window from every start
rows.timeWhy: Each start **rescans** characters the previous start already counted.
Counting t is **O(m)**; `left` and `right` each pass over s **once**.

blocks.text: This is the hardest of the window problems because it combines everything: counts with duplicates, a single number that says *valid or not*, and a shrink loop. If you can explain `missing`, you can do the rest.

items: **t longer than s**, or a character of t missing from s — `""`.
**Duplicates in t** — `t = "aa"` needs two a's in the window.
**The whole string is the answer** — the shrink loop must still record it.
**Upper and lower case** — `'a'` and `'A'` are different characters; a 26-slot array isn't enough.
**Smallest Range Covering Elements from K Lists** — the same grow/shrink window over a merged, sorted list.
**Minimum Size Subarray Sum** — the shortest window whose sum reaches a target: the same loop with a running sum instead of counts.
**Substring with Concatenation of All Words** — windows of whole words, stepping a word length at a time.
